I called the customer service line to let them know my issue and I asked if I can cancel or reschedule the flight they said unfortunately I would need to open a case and they would need to review. reviews.title: USD 778.50 to correct date of birth mistake on reservation that was not my fault
reviews.text: I recently booked Mexico City->Madrid->Mexico City->Tuxtla Gutierrez with the first two legs on Iberia and the final leg on Viva Aerobus. I did this all on Iberia's website as they have some sort of partnership with Viva Aerobus. Iberia's website has a problem where you can't select anything except for "1" for the passenger's day of birth. I saw that other people have had this problem and they called Iberia to get it corrected. However, in my case after I entered the passengers' passport information, I called Iberia and the agent told me that the birth dates were now correct. But they did not update on the Viva Aerobus leg according to their web site. I called Viva Aerobus and they told me that to change this mistake they would have to re-issue the tickets and I would have to pay a change fee of USD 370 plus tax for each ticket. How outrageous is this??? The change fee was greater than the cost of the domestic flight in Mexico but they calculated it based on the fact it was part of an expensive international booking. Why could Iberia update it easily at no cost but not Viva Aerobus? Both are "international" flights. Why do I feel like a robbery victim?

reviews.title: Trash company, lost my bag and illegally refused compensation
reviews.text: Avoid this airline at all costs! They lost my luggage, found it a day later and then made it very very hard to get the bag back. I was told that I was entitled to compensation for the purchases I made to replace essential items in the interim (since I received my bag almost a month later). This compensation is, in fact, required by US law. I bought minimal items to cover myself in the month, and then submitted a compensation claim with all receipts and information. They then REFUSED to compensate me, instead offering me travel credit amounting to significantly less than I had claimed! Imagine, travel credit with the airline that lost your baggage - an airline that only has flights on the other side of the world to where I live. It is just plain illegal to operate within the United States and not adhere to their laws. They really are just waiting to screw over the wrong person who actually decides to sue them. Let's hope that day comes soon.
